chapter: Brawls, the Ink Spots and boyhood recollections
title: The carnival's minstrel format and a cow-and-watch joke
summary: The black troupe did a minstrel show with an interlocutor and two end men; he recounts a joke and says it needed two people to deliver.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: which you had referred to earlier, you were with a black group of performers, right, there was one group -- troupe of black performers that were a part of the carnival; is that right?
And when the carnival performed, what role did you all play in it?
I know, but the whole group of black performers --
They did mostly like a minstrel thing -- you have an end man and an interlocuter.

That's the straight man that asks all the questions. He's called the interlocuter. And two end men, interlocuter and they have the rest of the people fill in like a chorus, you know, we all sang together, we all had jokes together.
Do you remember any of the jokes, the songs from that time?

Yeah, I remember a couple of the jokes. One of the jokes that says -- one fella says to the other fella, he says, "You know, Henry, I saw you go down the road there you had a cow on the end of your rope. Where were you going with that cow. Is that your cow?" "I had him, didn't I?" "Yeah, that ain't nothing, I heard about you, so what did you do?" "What did you hear about me?" "I heard that you was in a jewelry store and you stole a watch." "Who told you that?" "Oh, you know so-and-so, he told me." "Did he?" "Yeah, ole cowie, old watchie." So the guy who stole the watch says to the guy who has the cow, he says, "What time is it?" He says, "It's milking time." The way he had the line it was funny. Sure was funny. I laughed, I thought it was a funny gag. Course today it isn't as funny as it was then. Time marches on, you know.
What is it about today that wouldn't make that joke work today?

The two people to deliver it. Ain't any two people that could deliver it as the two people who did it. Just like you Moran and Mack, Amos 'n Andy, two people. One person can't do what two people do. Intonation is one thing, characterization is another, you know. That's what makes gags. Like I tell the gag to my partner and say, "Man why don't you pull your window shades down. I saw you kissing your wife." And the characterization of that is how you laugh. "Whatcha laughing about, I wasn't even home last night." That's the funniest gag I ever heard in my life. That guy's gotta be awfully dumb to just take a gag like that, you know. The audience used to roll at that joke. And I just loved to say it all the time. That's the way life goes. Let's get back to (whats'name.)
